ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18619, as amended through 2024), Articles 2, 4, 5, 5-2, and Article 8 of its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Secrecy (Act No. 5493, as amended); Commercial Act Articles 289 through 300; Financial Services Commission administrative guidance and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) implementation notices implementing FATF recommendations; Presidential Decree on Anti-Money-Laundering Counter-Financing of Terrorism.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Section of the District Court of the registered office location, administered under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel and mutually exclusive routes. Hague Apostille route: certified Court Registry original -> notarization by Korean notary where required -> Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (MoFA Apostille Division) -> submit to accepting authority. Consular Legalization route (only if destination is not an Apostille Convention member): certified Court Registry original -> MoFA legalization authentication -> legalization by the destination State's Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. Never chain apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Official Court Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ROS) and competent District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Two exclusive parallel pathways. If the destination state is an Apostille Contracting Party: Court Registry extract -> Korean notarial certification -> MoFA Apostille Office -> apostille only. If the destination state is not an Apostille Contracting Party: Court Registry extract -> MoFA authentication -> Consular legalization by the destination State's Seoul diplomatic mission only. No sequential apostille-plus-consular chain is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney Appointing Representative Director and Authorizing Signatures
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route: executed Board Resolution and PoA -> notarization by Korean notary -> Apostille by Republic of Korea MoFA -> accepted directly. Consular Legalization route: executed Board Resolution and PoA -> notarization -> MoFA authentication -> legalization by the destination State's Embassy or Consulate in Seoul. The two routes operate in parallel and are mutually exclusive; do not perform both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Incorporators and the Korean Notary Public before whom the instrument was executed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille member states: notarized Articles of Association -> Apostille from Korean MoFA -> direct submission. For non-member states: notarized Articles of Association -> MoFA legalization authentication -> consular legalization by the destination State's representative office in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank maintaining a corporate account or conducting know-your-customer verification of the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing bank is located in an Apostille Convention jurisdiction: bank officer signature -> notarization in country of origin -> Apostille by the competent authority of that country -> submission to Korean party. If the issuing bank is located in a non-member state: bank officer signature -> notarization -> authentication by the competent foreign ministry -> legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that origin country. Parallel routes only; never combine apostille and consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-engagement screening of every shareholder, director, ultimate beneficial owner, and signatory against the consolidated OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) watchlists, domestic publicly appointed official offenders list, and adverse media databases. Determine foreign and domestic politically exposed person status, including family members and close associates, using credible public sources and commercial databases with passport-verified identity data. Re-screen at least quarterly and immediately before every money movement or capital distribution. Any sanctions match triggers automatic refusal; any unexplained inconsistent beneficial ownership or high-risk jurisdiction flags require a Suspicious Transaction Report to KoFIU within 24 hours and enhanced due diligence under Article 5-2 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-ROS, Internet Registration System of the Supreme Court of Korea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Rules, a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) must be registered with a corporate name capable of display in Hangul. A foreign-language trade name may be used only as an auxiliary business name and must be transliterated into Hangul phonetically. The four-tier naming protocol is: first, confirm the company type suffix 'Yuhan Hoesa'; second, select a distinctive element free of prohibited or sensitive tokens; third, prepare an approved Hangul transliteration of the proposed English collectible trading card brand; fourth, verify equivalence between the English trading name and the Hangul transliteration in i-ROS and record the confirmation in a board resolution.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Designated Financial Institution affiliated token requiring FSC approval
Words implying state sponsorship or public authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry officer rejects the proposed name, the applicant must request the written reasons and file corrective amendments with the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office before the remaining reservation window expires. If rejection is upheld, the applicant files a written objection within two weeks under the Commercial Registration Rules to the competent registration court; a further remedy is an administrative appeal under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the court decision. When the rejection is based on a sensitive token requiring ministerial approval, the protocol requires simultaneous application for prior approval from the relevant ministry, trademark clearance in Korean and English, and a supplementary board resolution. Counsel will coordinate all filings and track time limits.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an ISIC 3240 collectible trading card publisher, a virtual office, commercial mailbox, or registered-agent-only address is rejected by Korean municipal tax offices and commercial banks because the entity needs a demonstrable physical place of business for VAT registration, customs filings, raw material import for holographic cold foil printing, and in-person know-your-customer verification. A physical office suite is required with the corporate name plate, independent access, a lease term exceeding twelve months, utility invoices in the company name, and personnel physically present during normal business hours. Co-working space is permissible only if it provides separate office signage, a dedicated mail receipt function, unconditional tax inspection access, and a lease arrangement that satisfies the local tax office's actual-place-of-business doctrine.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk is quantified as 55 percent within the first twelve months for this goods-producing trading card business. Mandatory checklist: corporate name plate at entrance, original lease agreement, electricity and water utility bills in company name, retained Articles of Association and statutory records at the registered office, evidence of regular business activity, availability of employees or an authorized manager, and no sharing of an office with unrelated entities. Municipal tax officers may inspect under local tax statutes and the Public Officials' Duties Act, and registry officers may verify through field visits; failure to produce the checklist yields administrative penalties and adverse bank scoring.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Chapter III (Articles 601 through 635) governing a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), together with Article 34 of the same Act and the Commercial Registration Act, Articles 2 and 17.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, operating through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporate Registration of Incorporation (Corporate Registration Application, Registration Form 1) together with the certified Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Korean law does not prescribe a statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. The total contributed capital set out in the Articles of Association must be fully subscribed and remitted, before incorporation registration, into a blocked temporary corporate nominee account opened in the company name at a Korean financial institution; the bank issues a certificate of deposit balance which must accompany the registration filing. Those funds are escrowed and cannot be withdrawn until issuance of the certificate of incorporation, after which the funds are released to the corporate operating account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, as the First Board of Directors Resolution of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company), adopted by unanimous written consent of the board of directors at a duly convened meeting, that: RECITING that the Company has been incorporated as a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Commercial Act, Act No. 1000, as amended, and that the initial membership interests and capital contributions have been validly subscribed for by the incorporator and fully paid into a corporate escrow account; NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The certificate of incorporation and the Articles of Association of the Company, containing the authorized capital, the total number of membership interests, the value per interest, and the names of initial interest holders, are ratified, confirmed, and accepted in their entirety. The full amount of the issued and paid-in capital of the Company is and shall remain deposited in the corporate escrow account at a licensed banking institution in Korea, and no member shall be released from the obligation to contribute funds, assets, or services as set out in the Articles of Association. 2. The registered office of the Company is adopted as the address stated in the Articles of Association, and the agent for service of process in Korea is duly designated. Any change of registered office shall be promptly filed with the Registry, and legal notices shall be served at the registered office. 3. The banking relationship of the Company is approved, and the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, or either of them under the joint-approval mechanism established by the board, are authorized to open, maintain, operate, close, and sign for any demand deposit, savings, or foreign currency bank account and any related electronic banking agreement in the true name of the Company at a Korean domestic bank, and to execute any corporate resolutions, account signature cards, and agreements required by the bank. 4. The following statutory officers are appointed to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until death, resignation, or removal: the Executive Director, the Chief Executive Officer, the Auditor where statutorily required, and the Company Secretary for legal filings. Their powers and duties are set forth in the Articles of Association and the applicable provisions of the Commercial Act. 5. All officers and members of the Company are directed to take all necessary steps to complete the full corporate registration, tax registration with the National Tax Service, and business authorization permits required for the Company manufacturing and collectible trading card operations, including industrial, environmental, fire safety, and occupational licensing permits. 6. Any director or authorized officer is irrevocably authorized to execute, deliver, and file any application, certificate, declaration, or agreement as may be necessary to give full force and effect to these resolutions, and to incur reasonable professional fees in connection with the formation and licensing procedures. This resolution is adopted on the date stated in the corporate minute book at the registered office and has full force and effect as though adopted at a physical meeting of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Name Reservation and Business Design Submission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IROS) and the Korean Intellectual Property Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Internet Registration Office, select the Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company type and enter the desired Korean corporate name, an English company name, a business purpose covering ISIC 3240 and collectible trading card publishing, and the address of the proposed registered office. The system will compare the requested name against registered domestic companies and reserve a non-conflicting name. Prior to filing, inspect the Korean Intellectual Property Office trademark database for any prior mark on the intended card series or brand. Download and preserve the name reservation certificate, because it must be used in all subsequent formation and licensing steps.
required_dossiers: Identification of incorporator (certified passport copy or foreign resident certificate)
Certificate of name reservation issued by IROS
Statement of initial share capital and business purpose
Power of attorney authorizing the local formation agent
Draft Articles of Association
Certificate of incorporation and apostille of any foreign corporate incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused because of collision with an existing company or trademark, submit three alternative names for review, correct the English transliteration, or appeal to the registration court; the incorporator may refile through IROS after receiving a formal written objection from the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Articles of Association, Signature Certification, and Capital Escrow Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public or certified authentication office and a licensed Korean commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Association in writing, confirming that the initial membership interests have been fully subscribed, and execute the document by all incorporators. The signatures of incorporators and, where the registration jurisdiction so requires, a notarial or certified authentication of directors powers of attorney must be completed, and the company seal code must be determined. Open a temporary deposit account at a Korean bank in the exact corporate name of Yuhan Hoesa, deposit the full subscribed capital, and obtain the bank balance certificate and proof of blocked status. No funds shall be disbursed before court registration; after registration, transfer funds into the regular corporate bank account under the joint signature authority approved by the board.
required_dossiers: Original Articles of Association signed by all incorporators
Notarized or certified authentication of signatures and powers of attorney
Identification documents of initial members and directors
Certificate of capital deposit or the blocked account balance certificate
Statement of bank account relationship and account ownership
Corporate seal registration pre-application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries beneficial ownership or source of funds, submit the ultimate ownership chart, AML statements, and supporting source documents; if the Articles contain defects, amend and re-execute the document and obtain a corrected notarial certificate before proceeding to the registration court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the local District Court via the Supreme Court IROS portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration electronically via IROS or in person at the relevant District Court Registration Division, submitting the certified Articles of Association, capital deposit balance certificate, name reservation certificate, directors and auditor appointment documents, and evidence of registered office. The registration officer examines compliance with Articles 601 through 635 of the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act, then enters the company into the commercial registry and issues the certificate of incorporation. Immediately after registration, pay the stamp and registration fees, obtain a certified corporate seal certificate, and file any notice required by the National Tax Service. Verify the accuracy of the corporate number, legal name, capital, and registered office designation on the official corporate extract.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate registration of incorporation on Form 1
Certified Articles of Association
Certificate of capital deposit balance
Name reservation certificate
Identity and appointment documents of directors, auditor, and company secretary
Proof of registered office address, such as lease agreement or written consent of the owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is queried or suspended, correct the stated deficiency within the court correction period and resubmit via IROS; if the registry challenges the registered office, provide a certified lease or landlord consent; if the form is filed with the wrong district court, transfer the case to the competent court and pay the applicable re-filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: National Tax Service Business Registration and Corporate Tax Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office through the Hometax portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a business registration certificate with the district tax office through Hometax within one month of incorporation. Enter the corporate operation for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and source withholding; designate the statutory representative; register the corporate seal card for tax filings; and establish electronic tax invoice issuance. For a physical manufacturing operation, list all factory sites, provide floor plans and lease evidence, and apply for business classification codes corresponding to ISIC 3240 and custom printing. Maintain an AML and KYC file to support all future bank account openings and merchant processing approvals for Stripe and Authorize.Net. After issuance, display the business registration certificate at the registered places of business and upload it to the tax and licensing portals.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Certified corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form
Lease agreement or proof of factory address
Identification and authority documents of the statutory representative
Bank account opening certificate and final corporate bank details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requires missing information, submit a corrected application within one week; if the field inspection cannot confirm the place of business, provide the utility contract and landlord consent; if the requested business classification is rejected, appeal to the National Tax Tribunal or request a reclassification with supporting production evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factory Establishment Report, Environmental Registration, Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal autonomous district office, Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation, National Fire Agency, and Ministry of Employment and Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the factory establishment report or permission from the local municipal office under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act. The report requires site location certification, building floor plan, proof of ownership or lease, and a manufacturing classification list. File the environmental registration for emitting facilities with the Korea Environment Corporation and the Ministry of Environment, including a discharge schedule for air pollutants, wastewater, and hazardous waste. Then complete the fire safety inspection with the National Fire Agency, install fire suppression and alarm systems, and obtain the civil defense fire safety certificate. No production line may operate until a workplace safety and health clearance is issued by the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Keep a compliance dossier for municipal, environmental, and labor inspections.
required_dossiers: Factory establishment report application and site location certification
Registered office and factory lease or ownership documents
Building floor plan and structural load certificate
Schedule of air and wastewater emitting facilities
Hazardous waste generation, storage, and disposal plan
Fire safety design plan and installation completion report
Occupational safety and health management plan and employer registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the factory report is returned because of land zoning restrictions, submit an individual factory site approval application or choose an alternative industrial district; if environmental classification is upgraded, prepare a mitigation plan and obtain prior permission; if the fire inspection identifies defects, correct all violations and request reinspection within fifteen days; for occupational issues, implement safety measures and resubmit the clearance file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and the local autonomous municipal district office responsible for factory establishment reports.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment Report and Manufacturing Business License covering security holographic cold foil printing and collectible trading card production.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration rather than a full EIA where total factory floor area is below 1,000 square meters and annual printing solvent consumption remains below one metric ton; where the floor area equals or exceeds 1,000 square meters, or annual solvent consumption is one metric ton or more, a small-scale environmental impact assessment prior consultation is required. Facilities below these thresholds are exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment but must still register air and wastewater emitting facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge permits require compliance with Korean effluent standards of pH 5.8 to 8.6, BOD below 30 mg/L, COD below 40 mg/L, total suspended solids below 40 mg/L, total nitrogen below 60 mg/L, and total phosphorus below 8 mg/L, except where municipal ordinances impose stricter local limits. Air emission standards require a volatile organic compound stack gas concentration at or below 40 mg/cubic meter, particulate matter at or below 30 mg/cubic meter, and no visible fugitive solvent mist beyond the permitted boundary. Hazardous waste such as waste printing inks, cleaning solvents, and heavy-metal foils must be stored in closed, labeled, impermeable containers and transferred to a licensed hazardous waste transporter under the electronic manifest system within 30 days; ground injection, dilution, and open burning are absolutely prohibited.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the National Fire Agency, including a manufacturing fire permit, civil defense performance certification for building occupancy, and structural load inspection. Workplace safety and health approval must be issued by the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering employer registration, mandatory safety training, machine guarding for printing presses as well as cutting and laminating equipment, chemical safety data sheets for inks and solvents, and emergency evacuation plans.

stage_2.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the National Fire Agency, including a manufacturing fire permit, civil defense performance certification for building occupancy, and structural load inspection. Workplace safety and health approval must be issued by the Ministry of Employment and Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, covering employer registration, mandatory safety training, machine guarding for printing presses as well as cutting and laminating equipment, chemical safety data sheets for inks and solvents, and emergency evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, online portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs duty and import VAT clearance are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS e-clearance portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Yuhan Hoesa (Korean limited liability company) owned directly or indirectly by non-residents, the entity must first complete formation at the relevant Korean court registration office; it must then apply for mandatory business registration with the district tax office of the NTS. Submit the court-issued certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, certificate of initial paid-in capital if any, board resolution appointing the Korean domestic business operator or tax representative, power of attorney, proof of Korean place of business (lease agreement or branch office registration), and the representative's identification/passport. The application is made through HomeTax (or at the NTS tax office with jurisdiction over the Korean place of business) under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act. The NTS issues a 10-digit Registered Business Number which is concurrently the VAT identification number and corporate income tax reference. If the foreign entity has no Korean place of business and only supplies imported digital/electronic services, it must use HomeTax's simplified non-resident VAT registration and appoint a domestic tax manager; if a foreign entity has a Korean fixed place of business, it must also file an 'opt-in' or ordinary registration and obtain a 10-digit business number. After VAT registration, the entity must apply to the Korea Customs Service via UNI-PASS for an exporter/importer code by submitting its business registration certificate. No notarization apostille is required for domestic NTS filings if the documents are in Korean; foreign documents need apostilled Korean translation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; the Republic of Korea has no check-the-box election for classification of local entities. A Yuhan Hoesa is statutorily taxed as a separate resident corporate taxpayer and a separate VAT taxable person. The only domestic 'election' addressing group tax burden is the consolidated/group taxation regime under the Corporation Tax Act, available to resident companies that meet the 100% parent-subsidiary ownership and lock-in requirements; it does not override separate entity classification for VAT or foreign entity treatment. Hybrid mismatch rules are applied through domestic deduction-disallowance rules for payments characterized inconsistently by another jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold; Korea mandates VAT/business tax registration from the first taxable business activity. Newly formed local businesses, including a Yuhan Hoesa, must register regardless of turnover. A smaller taxpayer with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million may be classed as a simplified taxpayer for filing/simplified invoice purposes, but this does not operate as an exemption or registration threshold. Non-resident suppliers of electronic services (e.g., digitally delivered content) must complete simplified VAT registration through HomeTax from the first B2C supply to Korean non-registered consumers; imported goods become subject to VAT automatically at customs clearance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory e-invoicing platform called HomeTax e-invoice (electronic tax invoice). VAT-registered suppliers must issue and transmit electronic tax invoices to the NTS for all B2B supply of goods or services. The NTS provides an open API and certified ERP interfaces for real-time secure transmission. There is no separate pre-approval fiscal stamp or third-party fiscal clearance authority, but the NTS real-time validates invoice numbers and matches invoice line items against VAT returns and customs export declarations. For retail cash sales to individuals, cash receipt devices are required, and consumers can verify receipts on HomeTax; receipts are transmitted to the NTS by the approved cash receipt service provider.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act applies to physically exported tangible goods, including collectible trading cards produced and sold to foreign customers, provided the goods are delivered outside Korea, move under a valid Korean customs export declaration, and are settled in foreign exchange in satisfaction of export-payment rules. Directly related services to exported goods (for example, custom security-holographic cold-foil design and printing work applied to goods that are physically exported) are also zero-rated if the service is supplied to a non-resident and the goods are exported. The seller must be registered with NTS and issue an electronic tax invoice marked as export zero-rated. If the supply takes place in Korea or the goods are ultimately used or consumed in Korea, the supply is not zero-rated and remains taxable at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Customs Clearance Status) issued through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS channel
Bill of Lading (for sea freight) or Air Waybill (for air freight) showing the Korean exporter as shipper
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the collectible trading cards and their export value
Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation (bank-issued Foreign Exchange Purchase/Receipt Certificate) demonstrating collection of export sale proceeds in convertible foreign currency
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice transmitted through HomeTax to the NTS
Sales contract or purchase order with the overseas buyer
Proof of the foreign buyer's non-resident status, such as its overseas tax registration or passport/trade license, when NTS requests additional evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS automatically reconciles HomeTax e-invoice data, UNI-PASS export declarations, and Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmations. If the exporter fails to provide the required customs declaration, transport document, or evidence of foreign exchange settlement within 180 days (or within an officially granted extension), the NTS will assess VAT at 10% on the gross supply amount. Negligent failure or omission triggers additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act and daily statutory interest; a fraudulent export invoice triggers additional tax of up to 100% of the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and criminal liability under the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Economic Crimes, including imprisonment and fines up to three times the evaded amount. Tax assessments for genuine omissions generally run for five years; deliberate fraudulent zero-rating claims extend the clawback window to ten years. Korea Customs Service may also impose customs penalties, interest, and seizure/confiscation for false export declarations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, jointly administered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with operational foreign exchange reporting executed through designated foreign exchange banks in Korea.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberalised yet notification-based foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions for trade in goods and services, including collectible trading card exports, licensing royalties, and e-commerce settlement inflows from Stripe or Authorize.Net, are fully convertible without prior central bank approval; however, every payment routed through a designated foreign exchange bank must be accompanied by a foreign exchange declaration (foreign exchange remittance justification form) evidencing the underlying commercial contract. Capital account transactions, including the non-resident equity injection into the Yuhan Hoesa LLC, require a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, after which the Bank of Korea automatically records the subscription and the commercial registry reflects the paid-in capital. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after a statutory external audit; banks will require a dividend resolution certified by the board, the audited financial statements, and a National Tax Service tax clearance certificate. In practice, conversion of KRW into USD, EUR, or JPY on the Seoul Money Brokerage market is unrestricted within licensed banking channels, but any single settlement exceeding USD 500,000 requires a supporting transaction file. For a collectible trading card manufacturer, royalty and license outflows to non-resident IP holders are treated as current account service payments subject to withholding tax reconciliation, and must satisfy arm's-length pricing documentation under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs to prevent disguised capital flight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The Republic of Korea has abolished mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Under Article 8 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Trading Guidelines, an exporter must settle export proceeds within 90 days from the date of the export declaration; settlement means the receipt, collection, and disposition of the foreign currency through a designated foreign exchange bank. The export receipt may remain in a foreign currency account without mandatory conversion to KRW. Extensions beyond the 90-day statutory window are available through the head of the relevant Korea Customs Service office for commercial disputes, inspections, or contractually deferred payment terms. Non-settlement without an approved exemption triggers administrative fines, automatic reporting to the Korea Customs Service and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), and may result in revocation of the exporter's trade-related banking privileges.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Trade Settlement Account
Trade Settlement Account and Foreign Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account and General Operational Account
Strategic Financing Facility Account for export-oriented manufacturing entities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border financial technology EMI servicing is Not Viable as a substitute for a domestic banking relationship. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the specific foreign exchange business guidelines issued by the FSS, non-bank electronic money institutions headquartered outside Korea (including Wise, Revolut, Neat, and similar EMIs) do not possess a license to open KRW-denominated domestic transaction accounts or provide Korean won clearing services to a Yuhan Hoesa LLC registered in Korea. Domestic digital banks (KakaoBank and Toss Bank) are subject to the same corporate onboarding and foreign exchange reporting obligations as commercial banks, but their foreign currency and cross-border trade finance product suites remain immature for corporate exporters. Stripe and Authorize.Net operate exclusively as card acquiring and payment gateway processors; they do not constitute banking rails and cannot replace the statutory foreign exchange declaration channel. The compliant architecture is to use a Tier-1 Korean commercial bank as the master settlement bank, with Stripe and Authorize.Net as incoming card acquiring rails that settle directly into the bank's foreign currency account under the merchant-of-record framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A mandatory physical presence is required. The statutory representative (chief executive officer or registered director) of the Yuhan Hoesa LLC must appear in person at the chosen Tier-1 bank branch to execute the corporate account opening mandate, present original identification documents, and complete the on-site AML interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for the initial corporate account or for the activation of foreign exchange trading privileges. After the initial in-branch onboarding, additional signing authorities and sub-account facilities may be registered under a notarised power of attorney with apostille or consular legalisation where the foreign director is domiciled outside Korea, provided the power of attorney is certified by the Korean consulate and translated into Korean by an accredited translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injection of offshore equity capital from a non-resident shareholder with opaque beneficial ownership layers, potentially triggering money-laundering red flags under the Specified Financial Transaction Information Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The shareholder must deliver a certified corporate registry extract from the home jurisdiction, audited financial statements for the last two years, bank references from the remitting account bank, a source-of-wealth declaration (salary, dividends, or prior disposal of assets), a structured ownership diagram identifying all natural persons owning 25% or more, and a formal investment undertaking submitted before the Korean bank's compliance unit; all documents must be notarised, apostilled or consular-legalised, and translated into Korean by a court-certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade document mismatches between the ISIC 3240 manufacturing scope, the HS classification of collectible trading cards, and the stated shipment value, triggering trade-based money laundering screening by the Korea Customs Service and KoFIU.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed bill of materials and production cost schedule, signed commercial contracts with overseas buyers, commercial invoices and packing lists, electronic export declarations with the relevant HS codes (typically 9504.40 or 4901.10), shipping documents (bill of lading/air waybill with container seal numbers), and a transaction-level reconciliation statement matching each received export payment to a customs declaration and a purchase order; store all records on the uTradeHub electronic trade platform for independent verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Settlement inflows from U.S.-based Stripe and Authorize.Net payment gateways lacking clear remitter identification, causing the bank's AML system to flag unidentified international credit card settlement credits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed merchant services agreement with Stripe and Authorize.Net, the gateway's settlement schedule showing Merchant ID and the payment processor's bank account details, monthly payment gateway transaction logs, chargeback histories, end-customer refund reports, a consumer privacy compliance statement aligning with the Korea Personal Information Protection Act, and a formal explanation of the reconciliation process between settlement files and the revenue ledger; this proves the funds arise from ordinary card-based e-commerce sales of collectible trading cards rather than from unidentifiable third-party remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty and licence fee outflows to a non-resident IP holding company creating potential structuring and tax-evasion concerns, particularly where the collectible trading card designs are owned offshore.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the fully executed intellectual property licensing agreement with precise royalty calculation formulas, ownership registrations for the relevant design and trademark portfolios, proof of economic substance of the licensor (office leases, staff lists, and audited financials), a transfer pricing benchmark study establishing arm's-length royalty rates using comparable uncontrolled transactions in the Asia-Pacific region, withholding tax clearance documentation prepared for the National Tax Service, and a statement of approval from the bank's foreign exchange desk confirming the payment purpose code for service and royalty settlements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection into KR_YUHANGHOESA should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's home bank to the designated foreign exchange bank in Korea under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The investor must file a foreign investment report with the receiving bank or KOTRA prior to receipt of funds; the bank issues a foreign investment certificate (foreign exchange purchase certificate) after the funds land and are credited to the capital escrow account. The funds are then converted into KRW at the onshore market rate on the same day, recorded in the company's paid-in capital ledger, and verified by a certified public accountant for the capital contribution verification certificate. For compliance, the SWIFT MT103 must include the investor legal entity identifier, the purpose code for equity capital injection, and an unambiguous beneficiary reference to the Yuhan Hoesa's corporate registration number. The foreign investment enterprise registration is then filed with the commercial registry and the relevant tax office, enabling the company to open trade settlement accounts and apply for subsequent foreign exchange banking facilities.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade disbursements tied to the collectible trading card manufacturing supply chain, SWIFT MT103 wire transfers are the standard clearing rail for high-frequency, low-value purchases of printing materials, UV coatings, holographic cold foil films, and packaging supplies; each outward transfer requires an invoice, purchase order, and a foreign exchange declaration matching the exact payment purpose code. For large procurement exceeding USD 50,000, commercial letters of credit (sight L/C or deferred L/C) are advised through the Korean bank using the MT700/MT710 SWIFT series, providing the supplier with bank-guaranteed settlement against presentation of shipping documents. Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) execute efficiently for recurring suppliers with an established transactional history, lowering issuance costs while retaining title control through the bank's negotiating channel. All outbound remittances to jurisdictions on the FATF grey list or with restricted financial transparency require additional economic substance documentation and may face extended compliance review by the bank's international banking division. Inbound card acquiring flows from Stripe and Authorize.Net settle in USD into the entity's foreign currency account; the bank's auto-fx daily conversion is recommended to minimise KRW exposure and to maintain a clean audit trail for the external auditor.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD spot-forwards with settlement tenors up to 12 months, executed on genuine underlying trade receivables or committed purchase orders, documented through the bank's trade finance desk
KRW/USD cross-currency swaps limited to capital structures where principal amortisation exceeds 12 months, providing synthetic KRW funding against multilateral development or parent-company loans

KRW/USD foreign exchange option collars (buy USD call and sell USD put) structured by the onshore dealing room, permitted only against an open export receivable book evidenced by purchase orders and shipping schedules

Over-the-counter non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible for the onshore Yuhan Hoesa entity as the company maintains legitimate KRW revenue and statutory trade documentation; offshore NDF execution is restricted by BOK transaction reporting rules and may be considered only upon a successful FSS waiver for residual tail risk on non-KRW operating currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal year ending on December 31, the corporate income tax return must be filed and taxes paid by March 31 of the following year. Interim prepayments are due by August 31 and December 31 of the current fiscal year for mid-year profits.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers: (a) a 20% penalty on the unpaid amount for fraudulent underreporting; (b) a 10% penalty on the unpaid amount for general non-filing or underreporting; (c) an additional daily late-payment interest equal to 0.03% of the unpaid tax per day of delay, or 0.06% after exceeding one month. Persistent failure to file for over six months may result in a tax delinquency seizure order and, for dormant entities, involuntary closure and administrative strike-off under the Corporate Registration Act and the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The first half VAT return (January 1 - June 30) must be filed and paid by July 25. The second half VAT return (July 1 - December 31) must be filed and paid by January 25 of the following year. For affected businesses, preliminary VAT payments are due by March 25 and September 25.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or deficient reporting incurs a surcharge of 0.03% of the unpaid tax per day from the due date. Submit kok box underreporting penalties are 10% of the unpaid amount; intentional concealment or fraud attracts a 20% penalty. Tax invoice issuance violations attract additional penalties of up to 1% per transaction. Continued non-compliance allows the NTS to estimate and assess tax with compulsory collection; persistent non-filing for over one year may trigger enforcement procedures and ultimately a request for administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via the DART electronic disclosure system; also filed with the National Tax Service as supporting documents for the corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If the entity meets the mandatory audit thresholds, the certified external auditor's report and audited financial statements must be submitted, where applicable, within 90 days after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year). For non-listed unlisted companies subject to audit, the deadline is simultaneous with the corporate income tax return due date of March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to commission an auditor or file the audit report may result in administrative fines up to KRW 50,000,000 (approximately USD 37,000). Company officers may be separately fined KRW 20,000,000 or more. Persistent non-compliance can trigger FSS inspection, criminal referral for negligence of statutory duties, and, in extraordinary cases, judicial dissolution or penalty for erroneous financial statements affecting tax assessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Changed Reporting and Annual Foreign-Invested Enterprise Status Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) and the designated foreign exchange bank under the Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in foreign investment status, share transfer, capital reduction, or reinvestment must be reported within 30 days from the occurrence of the event. For a foreign-invested company with a foreign equity interest equal to or above 10%, an annual foreign invested enterprise report must be submitted by January 31 of the following year to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA or the relevant foreign exchange bank.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unreported or late-reported foreign investment changes may be subject to administrative fines up to KRW 1,000,000. Deliberate misrepresentation may cause cancellation of foreign investment registration, loss of tax incentives and foreign investor protections, and fines under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Where share transfers are not reflected in the registry, shareholders may also face loss of dividend rights and inability to exercise voting rights.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, as amended and implementing decree, an independent statutory audit by a certified Korean Certified Public Accountant is compulsory for any yuhan hoesa (LLC) if it meets any of the following at the end of the preceding fiscal year: (a) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 8.89 million); (b) total revenue equals or exceeds KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.41 million) and average number of employees equals or exceeds 100; or (c) it is a company whose industry is newly designated by the Financial Services Commission as requiring audit to protect investors or for public interest. Additionally, an audit is required if the company is a public company listed on a Korean exchange, regardless of size, or if the company qualifies as a large conglomerate subject to external audit under the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act. For companies not meeting these thresholds, a review engagement (external review) may be required if total assets are between KRW 2 billion and KRW 12 billion, depending on revised thresholds effective under the Act. The audit is mandatory under strict vicarious liability and the company must appoint the auditor within 8 weeks after the fiscal year-end.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory for publicly traded companies and for companies subject to external audit whose total assets exceed KRW 120 billion. For unlisted companies not required to use K-IFRS, the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) as promulgated by the Korean IFRIC and the FSS are accepted, but K-IFRS may be voluntarily adopted. For small and medium enterprises not subject to external audit, the Korean Small and Medium Enterprise Accounting Standards (SME GAAP) may be applied.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information (AML law), there is no separate standalone annual UBO confirmation filing to the KOTRA or the NTS. However, the company must maintain an up-to-date register of its members in Korea. Any transfer of shares of a yuhan hoesa must be reported to the registry court through a shareholder transfer report within 30 days from the date of transfer; otherwise the transferee may not exercise voting rights or receive distributions. Foreign invested companies must report any beneficial ownership change to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank within 30 days. Financial institutions require updated beneficial ownership information at every transactional touchpoint under the Anti-Money Laundering rules; inaccurate records are subject to administrative fines up to KRW 50 million and criminal penalties for deliberate concealment.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Minutes of Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year for a registered office and company secretarial service in Seoul or a provincial office, converted at the reference rate of 1,350 KRW per USD
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 for a statutory audit of a yuhan hoesa that meets the mandatory audit threshold (asset-dependent and transaction-volume-dependent); if the entity is below the threshold and only needs an accountant's review report for tax or financing purposes, the typical fee range is USD 1,500 - USD 3,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income; 19% above KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion; plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the corporate income tax liability, producing combined effective headline rates from 9.9% to 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box regime exists; incentives are primarily statutory: Special Tax Treatment Control Law R&D and facility investment tax credits, SME and job-creation exemptions, and foreign-investment incentives under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act under which high-tech foreign enterprises in free economic zones or qualifying FDI can obtain up to 100% corporate income tax exemption for 5 years and a 50% exemption for the following 2 years, subject to ongoing local employment and substance conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return for Foreign Corporations (Corporate Tax Act Article 60) filed with the National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic filing portal; a Yuhan Hoesa with a domestic business place files the standard foreign-corporation corporate income tax return and calculation schedules together with financial statements, non-resident shareholder schedules, and transfer pricing attachments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with mid-year advance payment obligations; for a corporation with prior-year corporate income tax above the statutory threshold, the advance payment return is generally due within two months after the end of the first six months of the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Korean LLC the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following year, with the deadline extended to the next business day if it falls on a non-business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identity, foreign residency status, domestic place of business, and non-resident shareholder declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the LLC's Korean business registration number, head office address, direct foreign shareholder identities, residence countries, and ownership percentages. If no permanent establishment exists, only withholding obligations are reported; if a PE exists, all Korean-source income attributable to the PE must be reported. Attach the board resolution and leases/payroll records proving substantive Korean management and commercial premises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Korean-source gross income from collectible trading card sales, printing services, and royalty/licensing activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only income sourced in Korea under Corporate Tax Act Article 93: Korean card-manufacturing and printing revenue, income from the use of TCG intellectual property in Korea, and domestic publishing receipts. Separately disclose all cross-border related-party transactions and ensure amounts reconcile to the transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and arm's-length adjustment schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses substantiated by valid tax invoices, customs documents, contracts, and foreign-exchange records. Allocate head-office costs under the arm's-length principle; do not deduct offshore management fees lacking economic substance, inflated subcontract printing costs, or unapproved related-party service charges. Record all tax adjustments on the reconciliation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforwards, depreciation, and foreign tax credit adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Carry forward Korean-source net operating losses for up to 10 years; do not offset head-office or foreign-branch losses against the Korean PE's income. Apply the graduated corporate rate schedule. If foreign withholding tax is credited against Korean corporate income tax on export royalties, attach the foreign tax credit schedule and evidence of the foreign tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, non-resident dividend withholding reconciliation, and local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute R&D and facility-investment tax credits; reconcile withholding on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders during the tax year and report any unresolved treaty claims. Add local income tax at 10% of the national corporate income tax liability and state the combined final amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment summary, refund claim, and treaty relief schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the final corporate income tax, prior advance payments, additional payment due, or refund. If a reduced DTA rate on dividends, interest, or royalties is claimed, attach the non-resident treaty exemption/reduction application, Tax Residency Certificate, and beneficial ownership declaration; absent a complete pre-payment treaty claim, the 22% aggregate statutory withholding applies and refund recovery requires a separate administrative claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate income tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent non-filing; underreporting triggers 10% of the deficient tax, increased to 40% for fraudulent or grossly negligent underreporting under National Tax Basic Act Articles 47-2 through 47-5; unpaid tax additionally accrues a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022%. Intentional evasion by a director or beneficial owner is criminally punishable under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) by imprisonment up to 2 years and/or a fine up to twice the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national corporate income withholding plus a 2% local income tax surtax (10% surtax on the 20% national withholding), producing an aggregate statutory Korean dividend withholding tax rate of 22%, reduced only under an applicable Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief is not automatic. Before paying a dividend, the Korean LLC as withholding agent must obtain the foreign shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence state's competent authority, verify beneficial ownership through a current declaration and substance evidence, and file the prescribed Application Form for Tax Treaty Exemption/Reduction with the district tax office via HomeTax before payment. If the non-resident is a conduit or lacks economic substance, the statutory 22% withholding must be applied, and only the foreign beneficial owner can later pursue a refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border interest and intellectual property royalties is 20% national plus 2% local surtax, a 22% aggregate; treaty rates vary by DTA and performance. By illustration, the Korea-U.S. DTA commonly caps qualifying industrial royalties and interest at 10%, and direct corporate ownership dividends at 10% while portfolio dividends remain 15%, provided the beneficial owner files the required treaty forms. Intercompany debt must also satisfy Korean thin capitalization and interest-deduction limits, otherwise excess interest can be recharacterized as dividends and taxed at the dividend withholding rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Korea applies OECD-aligned documentation thresholds in KRW: CbC report is required when MNE group consolidated revenue is at least KRW 1 trillion; the Master File is generally required when the group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 100 billion; the Local File is required when annual cross-border related-party transactions reach the statutory KRW 50 billion threshold, with lower ministerial thresholds for certain intercompany services and intangibles. Even below these thresholds, contemporaneous arm's-length records must be maintained and submitted upon NTS request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: There is no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime in Korea, but the NTS applies the substance-over-form doctrine under National Tax Basic Act Article 14 and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule. A Yuhan Hoesa must possess real personnel, premises, books and records, decision-making authority, and business risks in Korea; shell arrangements will be disregarded and transactions recharacterized where core income-generating activities are not performed in Korea, particularly when testing permanent establishment status and treaty entitlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating or using false tax invoices for cold-foil printing materials and artwork services, recording overseas TCG sales revenue as non-taxable shareholder loans, or omitting Korean-source card royalty income from the corporate return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3(1) imposes imprisonment up to 2 years and/or a fine up to twice the evaded tax; National Tax Basic Act Article 47-3 adds a 40% corporate tax penalty for fraudulent understatement; the unpaid tax also accrues 0.022% daily.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where the Yuhan Hoesa is a mere facade or is used to commit fraud; directors can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, penalties, and third-party civil damages under Commercial Act Article 401, and can face NTS blacklisting, an overseas travel ban, asset attachment, and personal criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling TCG printing services, collectible cards, or intellectual property to a foreign related party at a non-arm's-length price, paying offshore related entities for no genuine services, or failing to prepare, retain, and submit the Korean Master File and Local File within the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs Articles 5 and 12 authorize the NTS to re-determine taxable income at the arm's-length price and deny deductions for missing documentation; National Tax Basic Act Article 47-3 can impose additional tax of 10% to 40% of the deficiency plus 0.022% daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing certificates or deliberately conceal related-party transactions are liable for resulting corporate losses under Commercial Act Article 401; the NTS may blacklist the directors, issue an overseas travel ban, and pursue personal assets, while criminal tax evasion sanctions apply if the false documentation is used to hide Korean-source profit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty Abuse and Withholding Evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Korean card-publishing royalties or dividend payouts through a zero-substance offshore entity solely to claim a reduced or zero DTA withholding rate, while the true beneficial owner is not disclosed and the Korean LLC continues to exercise management and CIGA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: National Tax Basic Act Article 14 (substance-over-form) and Article 15 (GAAR) allow the NTS to disregard the offshore conduit and reclassify the payment as dividend or royalty income taxable at the 22% aggregate withholding rate; Corporate Tax Act Article 98(1) imposes withholding liability on the Korean payer; false treaty claims trigger a 40% unfair underreporting penalty and 0.022% daily delinquency surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the Yuhan Hoesa is used as the alter ego of foreign principals to evade withholding tax, the corporate veil is pierced: directors and controlling shareholders become personally liable for unpaid withholding and penalties, personal assets can be attached, travel bans and blacklisting can be imposed, and criminal imprisonment for aiding and abetting tax evasion is available under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.
